title: Partial Results and Regular-Polygon Moment Obstruction for Erdős Problem #132 (Rare Planar Distances)
abstract: Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of partial results toward Erdős Problem #132 (rare planar distances: whether every n >= 5 points in ℝ² determine at least two distances occurring between 1 and n times). Using only propext, Quot.sound, and Classical.choice (no sorry, no native_decide), the repository proves unconditionally: (1) the Hopf–Pannwitz diameter theorem (fc_hopf_pannwitz); (2) sharpness at n = 4 via the unit rhombus (fc_four_points); (3) g(2) = 5, i.e., no 6-point planar 2-distance set exists (no_six_point_two_dist); (4) Erdős #132 for n = 5 and n = 6 via kernel-verified 3x3 Gram-minor integer Positivstellensatz certificates across all 1,024 K_5 edge 2-colorings and all 30 symmetric (1,7,7) 6-point extensions (fc_erdos_fishburn); and (5) a general m >= 4 regular-polygon 2nd/4th-moment obstruction theorem (no_regPoly_violator_extension, reducing impossibility to 3m > 9). Combining even-size endpoint descent with this unconditional moment obstruction yields fc_fourteen_of_wei_and_class13, which establishes a conditional reduction for n = 14 depending on two explicit hypotheses not proved here: Wei's bound g(6) = 13 (hwei) and the unproved 13-point <= 6-distance classification restricted to multiplicities <= 15 (hclass13). Both an unconditional resolution of n = 14 and the full conjecture for arbitrary n >= 5 (with the asymptotic growth question) remain open.
